description: Frame-codec round-trip obligation for the `json` REFERENCE codec (protocol.md § Frame codecs, #lzmsgpackparity). protocol.md states the codec requirement in prose — 'every fixture's frames MUST round-trip through both json and msgpack for all three IpcMessage variants' — and nothing tested it: the four conformance rungs all reason about fixture CONTENT replay, so a binding could carve a MUST-level codec out and stay green. This fixture makes the json half of that obligation executable. Each scenario pins one IpcMessage variant; a runner MUST decode `wire` under the json codec, RE-ENCODE the decoded message, DECODE it again, and evaluate every `expect` key against the SECOND decode — not against the fixture literal. A runner that asserts against `wire` itself proves nothing, because `wire` never passed through the codec. `round_trip_equals_source` is the runner's own computed decode(encode(decode(wire))) == decode(wire), so a codec that drops or mangles a field fails it. json is byte-canonical per codec (§ Frame codecs) but this fixture pins the DECODED VALUE, never a golden byte string, so the same runner shape ports to msgpack in frame_roundtrip_msgpack.json — the two fixtures carry identical `wire` values on purpose.

assertions.note: `role: reference` is the codec's ROLE — the required dependency-free interop floor every binding MUST speak, what the FFI baseline re-encodes to, what fixtures are written in. `byte_canonical` is a separate property of codec+message. protocol.md § Frame codecs keeps the two senses distinct; both are pinned here so a runner cannot conflate them.

scenarios.name: snapshot_frame_round_trips_json
scenarios.description: The `Snapshot` variant survives a json round trip with payload bytes, edges, roots, and the Opaque unit variant intact. `first_node_payload` is the discriminating field: a codec that re-encodes `Payload` as a base64 string or truncates the byte array fails it even though `node_count`/`epoch` still match. `opaque_node_state_tag` pins the externally-tagged UNIT variant, which is the shape most likely to decay into `{"Opaque": null}`.

scenarios.name: delta_frame_round_trips_json
scenarios.description: The `Delta` variant survives a json round trip across all seven DeltaOp variants. Op ORDER and op IDENTITY are the discriminating fields: a codec that re-encodes the externally-tagged op envelope as an internally-tagged `{"type": ...}` object, or reorders ops, fails `op_variants` even though `op_count` still matches.

scenarios.name: crdt_sync_frame_round_trips_json
scenarios.description: The `CrdtSync` variant survives a json round trip with its frontier stamps and its keyed/keyless op split intact. `WireStamp` uses `peer` (never `peer_id`). The optional `NodeKey` is the discriminating field: a self-describing codec OMITS `key` when absent (protocol.md § NodeKey), so a decoder must read an omitted key as absent and a re-encoder must not invent one.
